text: {"findings":[{"rule_id":"WF-008","evidence":[{"kind":"note","ref":"N1","page":1,"quote":"1) ALL JOINTS TO BE CO2 MIG, FULL WELDED.FILLET SIZE 10 mm."},{"kind":"note","ref":"N3","page":1,"quote":"3) SUITABLE EDGE PREPARATION TO BE DONE."}],"comment":"Note N1 calls for full welding but neither it nor note N3 dimensions the weld preparation (bevel angle, root gap). Without defined preparation geometry the welder cannot reliably achieve full penetration, risking an incomplete joint. The designer should add specific bevel angle and root gap dimensions to the drawing or replace 'SUITABLE EDGE PREPARATION' with a referenced standard detail that defines them.","recommended_correction":"Dimension the bevel angle and root gap for the full-penetration welds, or reference a specific standard weld-prep detail that provides those values."},{"rule_id":"NM-002","evidence":[{"kind":"note","ref":"N10","page":1,"quote":"10) TO BE TOUGHENED UPTO 28 ~32HRC"},{"kind":"note","ref":"N15","page":1,"quote":"H.T.PROCESS : TOUGHENED HARDNESS & DEPTH : 24 - 32 HRC. FINISH & DEPTH : ZINK BLACK PASSIVATION TRIVALENT TEST COUPON SIZE :(⌀25 x 50mm LENGTH - 02NOS) WELD CLASS : B IF APPLICABLE"}],"comment":"Note N10 specifies a hardness range of 28–32 HRC while note N15 on the same page specifies 24–32 HRC; these contradict each other. Conflicting hardness requirements will cause disagreement between manufacturing and inspection over whether the part is acceptable. The designer should reconcile the two notes to state a single, consistent hardness range.","recommended_correction":"Update either N10 or N15 so both specify the same hardness range (e.g., 28–32 HRC or 24–32 HRC)."}]}
